display.purpose: The one-sentence status answer on Home and the login intro line; key phrase steps to 800.

figure.purpose: Loan principal on loan cards; record figures use 750 at 1.5rem.

body.purpose: Running text; long explanations cap at 72ch with 1.6 line height.

label.purpose: Status chips, table headers, record terms. Sentence case, never uppercase.

wordmark.purpose: "Weenie Beanie" beside the bean token in the app bar and login.

shadows.name: shadow
shadows.purpose: Resting: panels, chart cards, beanstalk cards.

shadows.name: shadow-lift
shadows.purpose: Lifted: offer and loan cards, bell panel, toasts, presenter panel and toggle.

shadows.name: app-bar
shadows.purpose: The sticky navy app bar only.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default decelerating ease for all state transitions, popovers and growth.

motion.name: ease-in-drop
motion.purpose: The planting bean falling into the soil.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Colour, border and shadow changes on buttons, inputs, nav links; skip-link slide.

motion.name: duration-nudge
motion.purpose: Trailing link arrow slides 3px right on hover.

motion.name: rise
motion.value: opacity 0 → 1, translateY(8px) → 0; 220ms bell panel, 240ms presenter panel, 320ms toast

motion.name: bean-plant
motion.purpose: Bean drops 46px into the soil and fades.

motion.name: stalk-grow
motion.purpose: Stalk stroke draws up to its new height.

motion.name: leaf-unfurl
motion.purpose: New leaf scales from 0 at its base.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation and transition durations 1ms; beanstalk renders final state

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Two-column pages collapse to one; sticky asides become static.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Top nav hides; bottom tab bar appears; popovers become sheets.

breakpoints.name: bar-height
breakpoints.purpose: App bar height; offsets sticky elements.

narrative.overview:
Weenie Beanie dresses as a serious bank: a deep night-navy app bar, a cool near-white ground, white work surfaces with soft lifted shadows, and Manrope set tight with tabular figures. Inside that sober shell, the first thing on every customer screen is a plain sentence that answers "am I going to be OK?" at display size, with a shortfall amount, when there is one, set in red. Density is calm, not sparse: one answer, one chart, one decision card per viewport, separated by space and shadow rather than rules and boxes.

The one place the system becomes illustrative is the beanstalk. A hand-built SVG plant grows one segment and unfurls one leaf per on-time repayment, carries dashed tier marks at two and five leaves, and holds a tan bean beside the soil while a loan is open. Everything colourful in the product is tied to a meaning: green is growth, tan is the bean, red and amber are trouble. Navy does the rest of the work.

The system refuses the KPI-tile dashboard and the scroll-everything single page. It does not use a Capital One logo; the only reference is the footer line "Built on Capital One services". The product logo is in development, so the brand mark is the wordmark with the bean token.
keyCharacteristics: Navy shell, cool ground, white cards, soft two-level shadow.
The status sentence is the largest type on the page; a shortfall amount inside it turns red, a covered sentence stays ink.
Colour is semantic: green only for growth, tan only for the bean, red and amber only for shortfall, late and safeguard states.
One illustrated signature (the beanstalk); everything else is plain banking UI with Lucide line icons.
Motion is short and decelerating; growth is the only slow, celebratory animation, and it is static under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Growth Is Green Rule
rules.body: Green appears only where something grew or went right: the beanstalk, reached tiers, repaid loans, positive figures, the completed final step. It is never a generic "success" decoration or a brand accent.

rules.name: The Bean Is Tan Rule
rules.body: Tan belongs to the bean and nothing else. If a surface is tan, a bean is on it.

rules.name: The Alarm Budget Rule
rules.body: Red and amber appear only for shortfall, late, safeguard and default states. A calm screen has no red on it.

rules.name: The Answer Is the Headline Rule
rules.body: The display size is reserved for the status sentence that answers the customer's question. Nothing else on the page is larger.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every amount, date and count uses tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums), including chart axis ticks.

rules.name: The Two Heights Rule
rules.body: There are two card heights: resting for information, lifted for decisions and overlays. Do not invent a third.

dos: Do lead each customer screen with one plain sentence at Display size; only a shortfall amount inside it turns Red (at 800 weight), and a covered sentence stays Ink.
Do use Night Navy for the app bar and every primary action, and Harbour Navy for links.
Do separate cards with the Resting or Lifted shadow on Cool Ground, not with borders.
Do set every figure tabular, including chart ticks and table cells.
Do reference the CSS custom properties in frontend/src/index.css for colour; never re-type a hex in a component.
Do keep controls at 44px minimum height (36px small, 40px icon) and show the 3px Focus Blue ring on keyboard focus.
Do use Lucide line icons at 16–22px, inheriting the text colour unless a meaning colour applies.
Do honour reduced motion: the beanstalk renders its final state and all transitions collapse.
donts: Don't build KPI-tile dashboards or scroll-everything single pages; one answer, one chart, one decision.
Don't use green for anything that did not grow or succeed, or tan for anything that is not a bean.
Don't put red or amber on a calm screen.
Don't add uppercase labels, tracked-out eyebrows or kickers above headings; labels are sentence case at 0.8rem bold.
Don't add a third shadow height or put borders on cards.
Don't show a Capital One logo; the footer line "Built on Capital One services" is the only reference.
Don't let Presenter Slate or presenter controls leak into customer UI.
